tweets.text: A model can recommend the next move. That does not mean it should be allowed to authorize it.
Artemis separates evidence, policy, approval, execution, and audit instead of treating model confidence as authority.
The practical question is simple: where does authorization live when an agent can call tools?
Architecture and implementation map: https://www.clearglassinc.com/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=artemis_launch&utm_content=proof_thread
Technical criticism is welcome. Point to the trust boundary you would change first.
Agentic systems fail when policy exists only in prompts.
Artemis treats model output as untrusted data and keeps consequential authorization in deterministic controls outside the model.
That means typed tools, risk gates, explicit approval paths, provenance, and reversible deployment.
Review the live product surface and repository evidence: https://www.clearglassinc.com/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=artemis_launch&utm_content=security_thread
The standard is not 'does the demo work?' It is 'can the decision path be audited and reversed?'

threads.objective: Frame the repository as a product system

tweets.text: A repository earns adoption when a visitor can understand the problem, verify the proof, run the system, and know where to contribute.
That is why Artemis is being operated as a conversion funnel: discovery → README trust → live product → activation → contribution.
No fake stars. No bulk promotion. No invented customer proof. The growth engine is documentation, demos, releases, and useful technical artifacts.
Explore the current system: https://www.clearglassinc.com/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=artemis_launch&utm_content=founder_thread
If the quick start or architecture map creates friction, open a focused issue with the exact failing step.
The useful agent loop is not 'prompt → magic.'
It is evidence → bounded plan → policy check → approval where required → execution → audit.
That structure makes failures observable and recovery possible.
See how the pieces fit together: https://www.clearglassinc.com/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=artemis_launch&utm_content=automation_thread
If you adapt the pattern to another domain, document the trust boundary and failure mode. That is the contribution worth sharing.
Launch week is not the finish line. It is an evaluation window.
The useful signals are setup failures, architecture critiques, missing docs, reproducible bugs, and real integrations.
Stars are interest. They are not proof of adoption.
Start with the repository map and live platform: https://www.clearglassinc.com/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=artemis_launch&utm_content=contributor_thread
Contribute one focused improvement with verification evidence. That compounds better than engagement tricks.
